extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent attorneys/agents) before the USPTO and USPTO enrollment & discipline officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO (under 37 C.F.R. §11.24) when a practitioner has been disciplined by a state court, plus the duties and limitations imposed on a suspended practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state court (here, based on the Supreme Court of California's suspension) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director filed a "Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24" requesting suspension for two years with all but the first sixty (60) days stayed; the Final Order imposes suspension pursuant to this authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file a response within 40 days to contest imposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Notice and Order under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 is mailed, the respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information the respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order directed that a response must be filed within 40 days; respondent's failure to file leads the Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to impose the requested discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) via §10.23(c)(5) (state suspension grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Being suspended by a state supreme court (or equivalent) can constitute a violation of the USPTO ethical standard in 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) via §10.23(c)(5), providing grounds for reciprocal discipline before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the suspension was ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) via §10.23(c)(5) by being suspended by the Supreme Court of California.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of practitioner misconduct that predicated state discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misconduct findings that can support state suspension (and thus reciprocal USPTO discipline) include: failure to file a client's patent applications; failure to respond promptly to a client's emails and not informing the client of the status of its matters; misrepresenting the status of the client's matters to the client's new attorney; and failure to respond to State Bar letters concerning the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice/Official Gazette text lists these transgressions as the facts predicating the California suspension; such failures to perform, communicate, and cooperate with disciplinary investigations are actionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of suspension and stayed execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension from practice before the USPTO may be imposed for a fixed term (here, two years) with the execution of all but a defined initial period stayed (here, only the first sixty (60) days are actual suspension).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: suspended for two years, with all but the first sixty days of the suspension stayed; illustrates how the Office may mirror state-imposed terms including stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client business
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner subject to suspension may be granted limited recognition to practice for a short, specified period (here, beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days later) to wind up client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During limited recognition the respondent is directed to wind up all client business before the Office and withdraw from employment in pending proceedings; limited recognition explicitly expires after 30 days and the respondent is directed not to accept new clients during this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to withdraw from employment per 37 C.F.R. §10.40
rubrics_metrics.description: During the limited-recognition wind-up period, the respondent is directed to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly directs withdrawal and winding up 'in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.40', tying the wind-up process to the regulatory withdrawal rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: While granted limited recognition to wind up matters, the respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction accompanies the limited recognition period to prevent taking on new matters while finishing existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension, the practitioner, the reasons for discipline, and where disciplinary decisions are posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes the exact notice language to be published in the Official Gazette and cites the Office's Reading Room URL for public access to disciplinary decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 during the period of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs the respondent to 'comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 while suspended' (the order does not recite §11.58's text but makes compliance mandatory).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts under 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures inter-jurisdictional communication of public discipline; the Final Order specifically directs such notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement obligations under 37 C.F.R. §11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon any request for reinstatement, the respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order mandates adherence to the reinstatement procedures and requirements set forth in §11.60 when seeking reinstatement to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory authority including 35 U.S.C. §§2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and regulatory provisions such as 37 C.F.R. §§11.24 and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes and regulations as the legal basis for imposing and publicizing discipline.
